Amarillo by the numbers

Which county collects property tax on an Amarillo house?

The answer turns on the county line. Amarillo spans Potter County and Randall County, and each county's tax assessor-collector bills and collects for its own part, while a single appraisal district, the Potter-Randall Appraisal District, sets values for both.

The Comptroller's county directories list the offices and the taxing units that appear on an Amarillo bill: the City of Amarillo, Amarillo Independent School District, Amarillo Junior College District, the county itself and, depending on location, units such as Bushland ISD, River Road ISD, Highland Park ISD, Canyon ISD and High Plains Underground Water Conservation District No. 1.

  • Potter County Tax Assessor-Collector: 900 S. Polk St., Suite 106, Amarillo, phone 806-342-2600, mail to P.O. Box 2289, Amarillo 79105-2289.
  • Randall County Tax Assessor-Collector: 501 16th St., Suite 200, Canyon, phone 806-468-5540, mail to P.O. Box 997, Canyon 79015-0997.
  • Potter-Randall Appraisal District: 5701 Hollywood Rd., Amarillo, phone 806-358-1601, for values, exemptions and protests in both counties.

What is the City of Amarillo property tax rate?

The city's total rate is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation, made up of $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for existing debt. Council adopted it with the 2026/2027 budget in a 4-1 vote at a special meeting in late September 2026.

By the city's own count, the budget raises $2,063,963 more in property tax revenue than last year, a 2.58 percent increase, and $1,295,675 of that comes from property added to the roll this year. The city says the rate is effectively up 2.9 percent for maintenance and operations, which it puts at about $9 on a $100,000 home.

The same city page charts what Amarillo returns to businesses through economic development deals: property tax rebates under Chapter 311 and Chapter 380 agreements, and abatements under Chapter 312. For 2024/2025 it lists $1,143,899 abated by the city itself out of $2,959,496 abated by all participating taxing entities.

When are Amarillo property taxes due?

Bills are mailed around October 1, and most owners have until January 31. An unpaid balance on February 1 is delinquent, and that is when the 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are charged.

From there, the penalty goes up 1 percent a month through June and reaches 12 percent on July 1, with interest continuing at 1 percent a month. A taxing unit under an attorney contract can add up to 20 percent for collection. Owners 65 or older, disabled owners and disabled veterans may split a homestead bill into installments.

A homeowner who falls behind should call the Potter or Randall County office right away. Homestead payment plans of up to 36 months exist at some collectors. To seek a waiver of the penalty and interest, pay promptly and put the request in writing before day 181 after the delinquency date.

Which exemptions apply to Amarillo homeowners?

Texas lets a homeowner subtract $140,000 from the value used for school taxes, whether the district is Amarillo ISD or another that serves the address. People 65 or older or disabled get an added $60,000 for schools, and the school tax on their home is frozen at the first qualifying level.

Cities, counties and colleges may add local exemptions of up to 20 percent of value, so check which ones Amarillo, the two counties and Amarillo Junior College District have adopted. A disabled veteran's exemption runs from $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating up to $12,000 at 70 percent or more, and a 100 percent rating can exempt the whole residence homestead.

  • Applications go to the Potter-Randall Appraisal District, which handles both counties.
  • The general deadline is before May 1, though some veteran claims can be filed up to five years after the delinquency date.
  • Heirs not named on a recorded deed can claim a homestead with an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

How can an Amarillo owner protest the appraised value?

A written protest goes to the Potter-Randall Appraisal District. The cutoff is May 15, or 30 days after you receive the value notice when that falls later, and homestead notices start arriving about April 1.

The appraisal review board starts hearing cases about mid-May. Only the market value is open to challenge, since the appraisal district does not set rates. A homestead's assessed value can climb only 10 percent a year after the first qualifying year, even when market value jumps faster. A loss at the board leaves three paths: district court, binding arbitration, or, for values over $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

Because the appraisal district is one office for two counties, you do not file separately by county. Pay at least the undisputed amount to the Potter or Randall collector before the delinquency date while the protest is pending.

What should an Amarillo seller know about the local market?

Amarillo's July 2025 estimate from the Census Bureau is 205,130 people, compared with 200,393 in the 2020 count and 190,695 in 2010. The city covers 102.30 land square miles, about 1,958.8 people to each.

About 59.7 percent of homes are owner occupied, with a 2020 to 2024 median value of $196,900. Renters pay a median $1,092, owners with a mortgage $1,654 a month, and the median household earns $65,912. A bachelor's degree is held by 26.6 percent of adults, and the city has 10,973 veterans and 79,741 households averaging 2.50 people. Retail sales reached $5,722,271 thousand in 2022 and health care and social assistance receipts $2,777,390 thousand, while the average commute is 19.6 minutes. About 18.0 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance.

Census figures also show 89.2 percent of households with broadband and 11.0 percent of residents born outside the United States.

A Texas tax lien attaches on January 1 and follows the property, and the person who owned it that day stays liable even after a sale. Title cannot clear until back taxes are settled. If you owe both Potter and Randall accounts, for example on adjoining parcels, ask each tax office for a separate payoff letter before closing.

What happens if an Amarillo house is sold at a tax sale?

Texas lets the taxing units foreclose on the lien and auction the property, usually through the constable or an agent the unit hires. There is no statewide list of sales, so watch the Potter and Randall county sites and clerk postings.

A former owner may still get the house back for a limited time. For a homestead, farm or mineral interest, the redemption period is two years from the date the purchaser's deed is filed, and the redeeming owner pays the purchase price plus a 25 percent premium in the first year or 50 percent in the second, along with the recording fee, taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Other property has a 180-day window and a premium of no more than 25 percent. Money left after the sale belongs to the former owner for two years.

  • Ask the purchaser for an itemized list of costs; it is due within 10 days of a written request.
  • Keep every payoff letter, since taxes owed for different years are billed separately.
  • Call before January 31 if you can, because the penalty starts the next day.

More questions about Amarillo, TX Property Tax Guide

Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?

Both. The city lies across the two counties, so your bill comes from the county where the parcel sits. Potter-Randall Appraisal District values property in both.

What is the Amarillo city tax rate for 2026?

The adopted total is $0.43070 per $100 of valuation: $0.32412 for maintenance and operations and $0.10658 for debt. The budget raises $2,063,963 more in property tax revenue than last year's.

When do Amarillo property taxes go delinquent?

They go delinquent on February 1 after a January 31 due date. A 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest are added at once, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

Who do I call to pay Amarillo property taxes?

Call the county tax office for your parcel: Potter County at 806-342-2600 or Randall County at 806-468-5540. Use the Potter-Randall Appraisal District at 806-358-1601 for value and exemption questions.

How much is the homestead exemption in Amarillo?

The school district share drops by $140,000 of homestead value, and by $60,000 more for owners 65 or older or disabled. Cities and counties may layer on their own exemptions of up to 20 percent.

Brownsville by the numbers

Which offices value and bill a Brownsville house?

Cameron Appraisal District staff set the value, and the Cameron County Tax Assessor-Collector mails a single combined bill. That office also collects for the county, the schools, the cities and the special districts inside Cameron County, which means one payment covers every unit. Write to it at P.O. Box 952, Brownsville, TX 78522-0920, or call (956) 544-0800.

The appraisal district points out that people often confuse it with the tax office. It has no tax amounts and takes no payments, so bill questions go to the assessor-collector. The district keeps longer hours early in the week, 7:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Friday, and its website has a property search and a map search.

No state property tax exists in Texas, the Comptroller confirms, and each local unit picks its own rate. A house just across a school district line can therefore carry a noticeably different bill.

Which taxing units tax a Brownsville home, and at what 2026 rates?

For the 2026 tax year, the City of Brownsville adopted a rate of $0.603504 per $100 of taxable value, the same figure it adopted for 2025 and 2024. The table lists the units that levy on most Brownsville homes, as printed in the county's Truth in Taxation summary.

  • 2023 city rate: $0.607987, which the city's own notice described as a 12.13 percent drop from the year before
  • Brownsville ISD in 2022: $1.208690, compared with $0.771600 for 2026

Properties in a drainage district, municipal utility district or other special district pay an added levy, so check your bill for every line.

What are the due date and the late penalties for a Brownsville tax bill?

The collector mails bills around October 1, and payment is due by January 31. Taxes unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, and the Comptroller says a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added at that point. Cameron County's tax office describes the same hit as 7 percent penalty and interest on balances left after the deadline.

The penalty then rises one percent a month, and on July 1 it becomes 12 percent, with interest still growing at one percent a month. A unit that hires a private attorney can add up to 20 percent more. An owner can request a waiver of penalty and interest under Tax Code 33.011, which generally requires paying within 21 days of learning the bill was late.

The Cameron tax office offers a quarter pay plan for owners who are 65 or older, disabled, or a disabled veteran or surviving spouse of one, who claim a homestead:

  • First installment by January 31
  • Second installment by March 31
  • Third installment by May 31
  • Final installment by July 31

Online payment fees are posted by the office: $1.00 for an internet check of $5,000 or less, $3.00 for larger checks, and a 3 percent convenience fee on credit and debit cards.

What property tax relief can Brownsville homeowners claim?

The largest break is the residence homestead exemption. School districts must exempt $140,000 of a home's value, and owners aged 65 and up or with a disability receive $60,000 more against school taxes. The state also limits a homestead's yearly appraisal increase to 10 percent, and it holds the school tax on a senior's or disabled owner's home at the first qualifying amount.

A newer local option comes from the Brownsville Navigation District, known as the Port of Brownsville. In September 2026 the city posted that the district approved a 100 percent homestead exemption for qualifying homeowners who are 65 or older or have a qualifying disability, covering Brownsville, Rancho Viejo, Los Fresnos, Indian Lake and Starbase. It starts with the 2027 tax year, and owners apply through the appraisal district.

Disabled veterans may qualify for partial exemptions on a sliding scale, and a veteran with a 100 percent rating gets a full exemption on the homestead. File exemption applications with the appraisal district by April 30, using Form 50-114 for the homestead exemptions. Owners who inherit a home and are not on a recorded deed must supply an affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

How do I protest a Brownsville appraisal?

A written protest goes to the appraisal review board by May 15 or 30 days after the value notice arrives, whichever is later. Hearings start around May 15, per the Comptroller, and homestead notices are mailed on or about April 1.

If the board's ruling is not satisfactory, there are three further paths: district court, binding arbitration, or an appeal to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board's value is over $1,000,000. Anyone appealing must still pay the undisputed tax before the delinquency date, or the appeal can be lost.

Bring evidence to the hearing, such as recent sales of similar houses nearby, repair estimates and photos of defects. Ask the Cameron Appraisal District for its protest forms and hearing schedule when you file.

What is Brownsville like as a place to own a home?

Brownsville sits at the southernmost tip of Texas, facing Matamoros across the Rio Grande, and serves as the Cameron County seat. The Handbook of Texas traces the town to 1848, when Charles Stillman and a partner laid out a townsite next to Fort Brown. Brownsville became county seat on January 13, 1849, and the Brownsville Navigation District, which still levies a tax, was voted in during December 1928 to build the ship channel. The Port of Brownsville opened on May 15, 1936.

The University of Texas at Brownsville partnered with Texas Southmost College beginning in 1991, and the college district still has its own tax line. U.S. 77 and U.S. 83 end here, and Brownsville is a major port of entry to Mexico.

  • Mid-2025 estimate: 192,957 residents, 3.6 percent above the 2020 base
  • Typical owned home, 2020 to 2024 survey: valued at $139,900
  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 61.7 percent
  • Typical monthly rent: $923, with 3.13 people per household
  • Land area: 131.53 square miles

All five come from the QuickFacts column for Brownsville city.

Can a Brownsville house with unpaid tax still be sold?

Yes, because the title company asks the tax office for a payoff figure and settles the balance when the sale funds. The lien that attaches each January 1 secures that year's bill, and the January 1 owner stays personally liable for it after any later sale.

If the bill is already delinquent, ask the Cameron County tax office about a payment agreement. The Comptroller says some collectors allow up to 36 months on delinquent taxes, and that a plan is required for a residence homestead. Once a collection suit starts, court costs are added to the bill.

Tax foreclosure sales are public auctions, usually run by the constable or an agent for the taxing unit, and there is no statewide list. Check the Cameron County clerk and tax office sites for sale notices.

More questions about Brownsville, TX Property Tax Guide

What city rate applies to a Brownsville home for 2026?

The city adopted $0.603504 per $100 of taxable value, unchanged from 2025 and 2024. It is only the city's slice of the total bill.

On what date does a Brownsville tax bill go delinquent?

February 1 is the delinquency date for a bill left unpaid after January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest attach then, and the penalty climbs until it hits 12 percent on July 1.

Where does a Brownsville owner send the property tax payment?

To the Cameron County Tax Assessor-Collector, which bills and collects for the county, school district, city and special districts. The appraisal district takes no payments.

Do older Brownsville homeowners get extra exemptions?

Yes. Schools add $60,000 for owners 65 and up or disabled, on top of the $140,000 homestead exemption, and the Brownsville Navigation District approved a full exemption for them starting with the 2027 tax year.

What is the deadline to dispute a Brownsville appraisal?

May 15 or 30 days after the notice is delivered, whichever comes later. Send the written notice to the appraisal review board through the Cameron Appraisal District.

Killeen by the numbers

What rate does the city of Killeen charge?

Killeen's City Council adopted a property tax rate of 73.01 cents per $100 of taxable value for fiscal year 2027, which runs from October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027. The city's budget announcement splits the rate into maintenance and operations and debt service.

For a median-valued Killeen homestead, the city estimated a city property tax bill of $1,699.83, up about $68.48 from fiscal year 2026, or $5.71 a month. The city notes that actual bills depend on each property's taxable value and exemptions. This is only the city's share. The full bill adds Bell County, the school system and any special district over your address.

The same announcement puts the city's total fiscal year 2027 spending budget at $316.36 million, with a general fund of $137.24 million. The council approved a 3 percent cost-of-living adjustment for employees and water and sewer rate changes effective October 1. Read the rate and the budget as separate things: the rate tells you what a taxpayer owes per $100 of value, and the budget tells you where the money goes.

Which office handles value and payment for a Killeen house?

The Tax Appraisal District of Bell County handles both jobs for Killeen, and the city's property tax page sends you to its site, bellcad.org. That site covers property search, exemptions, payment options and truth-in-taxation information. Killeen sits in Bell County, so a Bell County parcel number opens any bill question.

Payment options on the district site:

  • Online or by phone with a card or check, where the vendor charges a fee. An electronic check costs $0.50.
  • In person at any location by check, cash or money order with no fee.
  • After hours at the Belton office through the outside drop box.

The district also lists early payment discounts of 3 percent through October 31, 2 percent through November 30 and 1 percent through December 31, shifting to Monday when a date lands on a weekend. Confirm the schedule on its site each fall before you count on a discount.

The district's home page also links a Truth in Taxation page with the latest rate information, a short explainer called "What's in my property tax bill," and a PDF on tax deferral. Read the deferral explainer before you assume it applies to your account. The district's property search also lets you view tax statements and amounts.

Killeen sellers should confirm that the homestead exemption they expect is actually on file. An exemption that was never filed is cheaper to fix before listing than at the closing table.

When does Killeen property tax become late?

Tax left unpaid after January 31 goes delinquent on February 1, with a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest that keeps rising into July. A collector that uses a private attorney can add up to 20 percent. The Bell CAD site also publishes its discount schedule, so paying in the fall can cost less than paying in January.

The January 1 lien explains why a payoff statement matters on a Killeen sale. Ask the district for the figure before closing, and ask whether this year's bill has been issued.

Help exists for an owner who is behind: a written penalty waiver request within 181 days of the delinquency date, four installments for seniors, disabled owners and disabled veterans on a homestead, and plans of up to 36 months where the collector offers them.

Which exemptions cut a Killeen tax bill?

Bell CAD says a homestead exemption is free to file, and it is the one most Killeen owners use. The district lists these qualifying exemptions:

  • Residence homestead
  • Disabled person
  • Age 65 or older, or a surviving spouse
  • 100 percent disabled veteran, or a surviving spouse
  • Surviving spouse of a service member killed in action
  • Surviving spouse of a first responder who died on duty
  • Donated residence of a partially disabled veteran, or a surviving spouse

The district asks for an updated driver's license or Texas ID, a Social Security Administration letter or A&B card for a disabled person, and a current or recent VA awards letter for a disabled veteran. It says no annual renewal is required, though the chief appraiser may ask for an updated application. Owners who file after April 30 are told to file anyway, and the district will provide any legislative remedy once the application is approved.

On top of the district's list sit the state school exemptions: $140,000 for a homestead and $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners. A disabled veteran's exemption runs from $5,000 up to $12,000 by rating, and a veteran rated 100 percent can receive a total exemption on the homestead.

How does the homestead cap work in Killeen?

Tax Code 23.23 limits a homestead's appraised value to a 10 percent yearly rise, starting the January 1 after the exemption first applies. The Bell CAD page calls those 10 percent steps mandatory until assessed value catches up with market value. A long-held Killeen home may therefore be taxed on a value well under market.

The cap does not follow the owner to a new house, and it resets in the sense that a buyer's value is measured fresh after a sale. Protests matter too. A protest of value is generally due in mid-May. Homestead appraisal notices are mailed around April 1.

For a senior or disabled owner, school tax is frozen at the first qualifying year's amount, and the ceiling can move in proportion to a new Texas homestead. A city or county may adopt a similar limit, so ask what applies to your account.

What do the federal numbers say about Killeen?

Federal estimates put Killeen at 161,883 residents in mid-2025, up 5.7 percent over the 2020 base, spread over 54.85 square miles of land. Owners occupy 49.5 percent of homes, so about half the housing is rented. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $215,400, and typical gross rent is $1,208. Middle household income is $60,977, and 23,452 residents are veterans.

The city describes itself as a military-heritage community with over 160,000 residents, founded in 1882. Veteran households make the disabled veteran exemptions above worth checking. The city's fiscal year 2027 capital plan includes $12 million for Stagecoach Road reconstruction, $3.1 million for Rancier Drive reconstruction and $610,000 for low-water crossing flood mitigation, which may interest a seller whose street is on the list.

More questions about Killeen, TX Property Tax Guide

What did Killeen adopt as its city rate?

The adopted fiscal year 2027 rate is 73.01 cents per $100 of taxable value, made up of 55.62 cents for maintenance and operations and 17.39 cents for debt service. County, school and special district rates are added on the same bill.

Who do I pay Killeen property tax to?

Pay through the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County, which lists online, phone and in-person options and a drop box at its Belton office. Match the parcel and account number on your bill to the district's property search before you send money.

When is Killeen property tax delinquent?

February 1 is the first delinquent day for tax unpaid after January 31, and a penalty and interest start that day and keep growing into July.

Does Bell County give a discount for early payment?

Yes. The district lists a 3 percent discount through October 31, 2 percent through November 30 and 1 percent through December 31, and a weekend deadline moves to Monday.

Where is a Killeen homestead exemption filed?

File the free application with the Tax Appraisal District of Bell County. Bring a current driver's license or Texas ID, and add disability or VA paperwork if it applies. No yearly renewal is required.

The page also records a 2024 city rate of 0.69000 and a 2024 school rate of 1.09920. A footnote cautions that other taxing units may be added to the totals, so look up your own parcel at the appraisal district before quoting a figure.

What happens after January 31 in Mesquite?

Statements are mailed in October and can be paid on arrival. Dallas County treats an account as late once January 31 has gone by, and it reads the postmark on a mailed check. Not receiving the statement does not excuse the tax or the late charges.

The Comptroller says the first day of February brings a penalty of 6 percent plus interest of 1 percent. Interest keeps adding a point a month with no stopping point, and the penalty rises a point a month until it tops out at 12 percent in July.

  • Dallas County hands non-business accounts to its collection attorney on July 1, and the attorney's fee can reach 20 percent.
  • To ask for a waiver of the charges, send the request in writing before day 181 of delinquency and settle the tax within 21 days of finding out it was late.
  • Some collectors write instalment agreements running as long as 36 months, and a residence homestead is the only case where one must be offered.
  • Seniors and disabled owners may split the bill into four payments.

How can a Mesquite owner shrink the bill?

Start with age. The city page lists a $65,000 exemption for homeowners over 65 and a $15,000 exemption for disabled persons, and a person gets one or the other. Either one also brings a ceiling: the city and school taxes stay at what you paid in the first qualifying year until you build onto the house or move.

School taxes have a state-set break of their own, $140,000 off a residence homestead and $60,000 more for older or disabled owners.

  • Disabled veterans exempt $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating, rising to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent, and a 100 percent rating can wipe out the homestead's taxable value.
  • A homestead's appraised value is capped at a 10 percent yearly rise, beginning the year after the first exemption.
  • Heirs whose names are not on the recorded deed send the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

When must a Mesquite owner file a value protest?

File the written protest with the Appraisal Review Board by May 15, or 30 days after delivery of the notice when that is later. Homestead notices start going out around April 1, and notices for other property follow near May 1.

Dallas County's tax office refers all protest questions to the appraisal districts, so a Dallas County parcel is disputed at Dallas Central Appraisal District and a Kaufman County parcel at Kaufman Central Appraisal District. Owners who lose at the board have further routes: district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values above $1,000,000. Pay the portion nobody disputes before the cutoff, or the appeal will not protect you from penalties.

How big is Mesquite, according to the Census?

Census QuickFacts describes a city whose headcount has barely moved since 2020:

  • Population: 150,693 in the July 2025 estimate, 150,108 in the 2020 census, 139,824 in 2010.
  • Size: 48.48 square miles of land, which held 3,096.1 people a mile in 2020.
  • Ownership: 62.8 percent of homes are lived in by their owners (2020-2024 survey), and the midpoint value is $245,700.
  • Money: gross rent at the midpoint is $1,513 and household income at the midpoint is $72,537.
  • Households: 50,171, averaging 2.96 people.
  • Commute: 32.1 minutes on average.
  • Age: 11.3 percent of residents are 65 or older, the people eligible for the city's larger exemption.

What should a Mesquite seller check before closing?

The tax lien keys off who owns the house on January 1. Whoever holds title that day owes the whole year, even when the sale closes in March. Ask the title company how the bill will be divided with the buyer, and read the payoff lines of its commitment.

A buyer closing after the new year may apply for the homestead exemption immediately if the seller never had it. Sellers should confirm what is owed with the Dallas County Tax Office, or the Kaufman County tax office for a Kaufman parcel.

When the account has already gone to the collection attorney, ask for a written payoff itemizing penalty, interest and court costs. The title company needs that figure to clear the lien when the sale funds.

Before you list, gather the latest statement from each taxing unit, your homestead exemption confirmation if you have one, and any protest paperwork from the spring. Tell the title company if a protest is still open, since a successful one changes the tax figure that the closing statement is built around, and note the hearing date for the buyer.

More questions about Mesquite, TX Property Tax Guide

Why does the Kaufman County side of Mesquite show a higher total rate?

Only the county line changes. The city's table shows 0.2155000 for Dallas County and 0.4275260 for Kaufman County, which produces printed totals of 2.3456670 and 2.5576930.

Until what date can Mesquite taxes be paid without charges?

January 31, per Dallas County. Charges begin February 1 and grow each month into July.

How much does Mesquite exempt for homeowners over 65?

$65,000 for owners over 65 and $15,000 for disabled persons, per the city, and one person gets only one of the two. Mesquite ISD applies its own state-mandated amounts.

Where do I pick up a homestead exemption form for a house in Mesquite?

Call the appraisal district for your county, Dallas Central at 214-631-0520 or Kaufman Central at 972-932-6081. The city's tax office does not issue them.

Can a Mesquite house with unpaid taxes still be sold?

Yes. The title company gets a payoff from the collection attorney and pays it at closing, since the lien follows the property until then.

Which offices handle property tax for McAllen homes?

McAllen sits in Hidalgo County, and a McAllen bill usually stacks the city, the county, a school district such as McAllen ISD and South Texas College, with special districts on some parcels. Values come from the Hidalgo County Appraisal District, while the City of McAllen Tax Office sends the city's own statement. For ownership or mailing address changes, the city's FAQ sends owners to the appraisal district at 4405 Professional Drive, Edinburg, TX 78539, telephone (956) 381-8466.

Hidalgo County's 2025 rate schedule prints these rates per $100 of value for the other units that tax McAllen property:

  • Hidalgo County: $0.57500
  • McAllen ISD: $0.93220
  • South Texas College: $0.16200

What is the McAllen payment deadline, and what does paying late cost?

Texas gives McAllen owners until January 31 to pay. According to the city's FAQ, a deadline that falls on a weekend slides to the following business day, and statements are usually mailed in October. For the 2026 bill, the last penalty-free day is therefore Monday, February 1, 2027.

Charges start on February 1. The city's FAQ prints this schedule of penalty and interest, and interest adds one percentage point each month until the account is paid. The schedule continues past July, reaching a 24 percent total the following January.

The city's public hearing notice proposes $0.448989 per $100 for 2026, matching the 2025 figure. It prints a no-new-revenue rate of $0.444778 and a voter-approval rate of $0.517054, and says the proposal is under the voter-approval ceiling, so no election is needed.

To learn which rate the commission adopted, call the tax office at (956) 681-1330. The notice also gives an average homestead taxable value of $217,661 for 2025 and $221,213 for 2026, with the total levy on all properties falling 1.10 percent.

The city's slice is one piece of the total, because the county, school district and college each adopt their own rates every fall. The Comptroller's calendar gives units until about September 29, or 60 days after they receive the certified roll if that is later.

Which exemptions reduce a McAllen property tax bill?

McAllen's own exemption list reads $10,000 for each owner who has reached 65, $10,000 for a disabled person, and $5,000 to $12,000 for a disabled veteran depending on rating, with a 100 percent disabled veteran's residence homestead fully exempt. The tax office page directs applications and address corrections to the chief appraiser at the Hidalgo County Appraisal District.

  • School homestead: the county's schedule lists $140,000 of value removed for McAllen ISD taxes on a residence homestead.
  • Older or disabled owners: $60,000 more off school taxes, and the school tax bill on that home generally cannot climb after the owner qualifies.
  • Value cap: a homestead's appraised value may climb at most 10 percent per year, with the limit starting the January after the exemption begins.
  • Filing window: most exemption applications are due before May 1, though disabled veterans may apply later.

Someone who buys after January 1 can sometimes claim the exemption right away if the seller never received it.

How can I pay in installments or avoid late fees in McAllen?

An owner who is 65 or over, disabled, or a disabled veteran, and who holds a homestead exemption, can split the bill into four equal parts free of penalty and interest by requesting it no later than January 31. The parts fall due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. The same group may seek a tax deferral, and while one is in force the taxing unit cannot collect against or foreclose on the home the owner lives in.

  • Mail: send a check or money order to City of McAllen Tax Office, P.O. Box 220, and no convenience fee applies. Mail postmarked by the delinquency date is treated as timely.
  • Online: a card payment carries a $3.00 fee when the total is $100.00 or less and a 3 percent fee on larger amounts. An eCheck carries a flat service fee that runs from $3.00 on small bills up to $30.00 on bills of $15,000.01 or more.
  • Drop box: the tax office has payment flaps, one inside the lobby and one outside on the Cedar Avenue side of the building. Put the payment and a copy of your statement in a sealed envelope, and leave cash out.
  • Email bills: owners who enroll in eNotification before October 17 get that year's bill by email.

When a mortgage company pays from escrow, it is the lender's job to tell the tax office which accounts it covers, and unpaid accounts get a courtesy reminder in mid-January. Never receiving the bill does not waive the penalty.

How does a McAllen owner protest an appraisal?

A protest must reach the Hidalgo County appraisal review board by May 15 or, when your notice arrives late, within 30 days of its delivery. Notices for homesteads are mailed about April 1 and for other property about May 1, and the Comptroller says hearings begin around mid-May.

After the board rules, an owner can sue in district court, ask for binding arbitration, or, for values above $1,000,000, take the case to SOAH, the State Office of Administrative Hearings. An appeal generally stays valid only if the undisputed portion of the tax is paid before it turns delinquent.

What kind of city is McAllen for a seller?

McAllen lies on U.S. Highway 83 about sixteen miles west of Weslaco in southern Hidalgo County. The Handbook of Texas traces it to Spanish land grants, the McAllen Ranch and the McAllen Townsite Company of 1904, when the railroad reached the area. The town received its charter in 1911, gained home rule status in 1927 and picked up the nickname City of Palms. International trade, winter visitors and the Reynosa bridge shaped its growth.

McAllen had 150,640 people at mid-2025 by Census Bureau estimate, compared with 142,210 in the 2020 census, spread over 62.31 square miles. Census survey years 2020 through 2024 tally 48,905 households; 59.5 percent of homes are lived in by their owners and a middle value is $190,400. Mortgage holders report monthly costs near $1,764, renters pay about $1,049, and household income centers on $61,579.

What if I owe McAllen property tax and want to sell?

Back taxes are normally cleared at closing, because delinquent taxes stand in the way of a clean title. Each January 1 a lien for that year's tax takes hold, and whoever owns the house that day stays liable for the year's tax after a sale.

Texas offers some relief before things reach that point. Penalty and interest can sometimes be waived: the request goes in writing before day 181 after delinquency, and the tax itself must be paid within 21 days of the owner learning of the debt. Certain collectors allow plans stretching to 36 months, and a residence homestead must be offered one. The city's FAQ lists the Hidalgo County office of a collection law firm at Lone Star Plaza, 1512 S Lone Star Wy, Edinburg, (956) 383-4500, for questions about delinquent notices.

Behind on the bill and thinking of a fast as-is sale? Send the property address and the balance on your statement.

When are McAllen property taxes due?

January 31 is the annual deadline, and a weekend date slides to the next business day. Penalties begin the day after the deadline.

Does McAllen offer a homeowner exemption?

The City lists $10,000 for owners 65 or older and $10,000 for disabled persons, plus disabled veteran exemptions. It lists no percentage homestead exemption. McAllen ISD applies the statewide $140,000 residence homestead exemption.

Can I pay McAllen property taxes in installments?

Yes, for homeowners past 65, disabled homeowners and disabled veterans who hold a residence homestead exemption and ask by January 31. Four equal payments fall due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31.

Value questions go to the Hidalgo County Appraisal District at (956) 381-8466, and the City of McAllen Tax Office handles billing at (956) 681-1330.

Card payments carry a 2.19% fee and electronic checks a $1.50 flat fee, both going to the payment vendor. Credit card payments need only the account number. An electronic check needs the account number and bank details. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and American Express are accepted.

The tax office runs tax sales online through GovEase, and bidders register there. An owner facing a sale should ask the tax office about redemption, which Texas limits by property type.

Evidence is posted in the online portal, which you reach with the property owner ID and PIN printed on the notice. What happens to the tax bill if I sell in Waco?

A lien for the year's tax exists from January 1, so the title company settles it at closing and prorates the rest.

The district's FAQ says the notice describes the property, shows its value and exemptions, and estimates the tax. Values shift when comparable sales move or when a record is corrected for a measurement or a pool, so read the description line by line before you protest.

After the board rules, an unhappy owner may take the matter to district court or binding arbitration, or to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the board value exceeds $1,000,000. The district reappraises every property at least every three years, and a qualified homestead's value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, starting the year after the first exemption.

How has Midland grown?

Census QuickFacts shows a city that added residents quickly after 2020:

  • Population: 147,615 in the July 2025 estimate, up 11.1 percent from the 2020 estimates base. The 2020 census counted 132,524 and the 2010 census 111,147.
  • Area: 75.45 square miles of land, or 1,756.4 residents a mile in 2020.
  • Ownership: 65.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied (2020-2024), with a midpoint value of $319,200.
  • Monthly costs: $2,205 for owners with a mortgage, $766 without one, and $1,434 for renters.
  • Income: $89,585 for the median household, with 53,414 households in total.
  • Age: 10.1 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Those figures cover the whole city. Individual streets can run well above or below them, which is why the appraisal district's own record for your parcel matters more than any average.

What should a Midland seller do about property tax?

Pull your account from the appraisal district before listing, because the same office values the house and sends the bill. The tax lien attaches each January 1, so the owner on that date is on the hook for that year even if the deed changes hands soon after.

  • Ask the title company how that year's tax is being split with the buyer.
  • Tell the buyer to file a homestead application of their own, since the exemption on file belongs to the January 1 owner.
  • On a delinquent account, request a payoff that lists penalty, interest and any attorney fee.
  • For an inherited house, heirs not named on a recorded deed give the district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the exemption.

Because Midland's rates rose between 2025 and 2026 while the school rate held steady, a buyer comparing your 2026 statement with an older one will see a higher city share. Keep both years' statements handy, and point the buyer to the district's rate page so the numbers come from the source.

What is Midland's city tax rate for 2026?

The 2026 tax year rate is $0.383092 per $100 of taxable value for the City of Midland, up from $0.347999 in 2025, according to the appraisal district. The school, county, college and hospital rates add to it.

Who sends Midland County tax statements?

The Midland Central Appraisal District mails them, and you can reach it at 4631 Andrews Hwy or 432-699-4991. For a Martin County parcel, ask the Martin County tax office.

Does the City of Midland grant a regular homestead exemption?

Not according to the district's table, which lists only $8,000 for owners 65 or older at the city level. Midland ISD gives $140,000 on a homestead.

Is it too late to claim a homestead exemption I forgot?

Possibly not. The district says a late application is accepted up to one year after the taxes become delinquent, and you have to file it yourself.

What does missing the January 31 date cost in Midland?

The Comptroller lists a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest from February 1, with the penalty reaching 12 percent in July and interest continuing monthly. An attorney fee up to 20 percent may follow.

The first settlement stood by a natural ford on Brushy Creek, near the round rock that gave the town its name, and the post office was renamed Round Rock in 1854 because another community already used Brushy. The railroad era created a second, newer downtown in 1876, and a first zoning ordinance followed in 1969.

Water has been both a limit and a hazard. A prolonged drought in 1978 dried up local wells, and in 1981 a 30-inch line from Lake Georgetown secured the supply. Dell's 1994 move of its world headquarters to the city brought, in the city's words, a significant jump in the tax base. Hospitals, a Texas State nursing campus and Austin Community College followed through 2010.

Each year's tax lien forms on January 1 and rides with the house. A buyer cannot get clean title until delinquent balances are cleared, and the January 1 owner remains answerable for that year even after the transfer.

You can send the protest form by mail, email to arbprotest@cadtx.org, the drop box, or the district's online portal after setting up an account. Market value is the only thing you can protest, not the tax rate. A homestead's assessed value is held to 10 percent growth a year. If you lose before the board, the next steps are district court, binding arbitration, or the State Office of Administrative Hearings for values over $1,000,000.

Which office bills property tax in Pearland, TX?

Your parcel's county decides. Pearland spreads across Brazoria County and Fort Bend County, and the Texas Comptroller's directory lists the City of Pearland as an active taxing unit in both appraisal districts.

Brazoria County's tax office, at 451 N. Velasco St. in Angleton, lists the City of Pearland and Pearland ISD among the units it collects for. Its phone number is 979-864-1320. The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, which sets values, is at 500 N. Chenango St. in Angleton and answers at 979-849-7792. For a Fort Bend County address, the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District is at 2801 B.F. Terry Blvd. in Rosenberg, 281-344-8623. Fort Bend County's own collection list does not include Pearland, so ask where a Fort Bend-side parcel pays.

Expect more than the city and school lines on a bill. The Brazoria list includes Pearland Municipal Management District #2, Alvin Community College District, Brazoria County emergency districts, drainage districts and dozens of numbered municipal utility districts. A newer subdivision often carries a utility district charge that an older one does not.

Schools differ by address too. Brazoria County's list includes Pearland ISD, Alvin ISD and Friendswood ISD, so the school line on your own bill shows which district charges your street.

What did Pearland's 2026 tax rate notice say?

In its 2026 notice the city lists $0.637892 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.693542 as the voter-approval rate, both per $100 of value. The lower figure would collect the same total as last year from property taxed in both years. The higher one is, in most cases, the most a city may adopt without calling an election.

What dates matter for Pearland property owners each year?

Every Texas taxing unit works from a single statewide calendar, and the anchor is New Year's Day: the property's value, and the person who owns it, are frozen as of January 1 for that tax year.

  • January 1: value is set, and that year's lien takes hold.
  • April 1 or soon after: appraisal notices go out for single-family homesteads. Other property follows around May 1.
  • Before May 1: apply for most exemptions.
  • May 15 (or the 30th day after delivery of the notice, if that is later): last day to protest.
  • July 25: the appraisal roll is certified and sent to every taxing unit.
  • September 29 or thereabouts: last day for units to adopt rates.
  • October: bills are mailed. Tax is due by January 31 and delinquent February 1.

A late account picks up six percent in penalty and one percent in interest on the first day of February. After that the penalty gains a point per month until July 1, when it sits at 12 percent, while interest goes on at a point a month. A lawyer's collection fee of up to 20 percent is possible where the unit has such a contract.

Protest hearings before the appraisal review board begin around May 15, and the board is expected to approve the records by July 20 unless more than five percent of total value is still under protest. Save the envelope or delivery record for the appraisal notice, since a late delivery moves your protest deadline.

How do Pearland homeowners reduce the bill?

File for the homestead exemption in the first year you live in the house as your main home. The school district takes $140,000 off the value for its own tax, and a homeowner who is 65 or older or disabled gets $60,000 further. City and county governments can adopt a percentage exemption of their own, up to 20 percent of value with a $5,000 minimum. Ask Pearland whether it has, since the Brazoria directory lists the units without their exemption choices.

A homestead also gets a growth brake. Beginning the January after the exemption is first granted, its appraised value may not climb by more than 10 percent per year. Seniors and disabled owners can additionally hold their school tax at a ceiling that travels with them to a new Texas homestead.

Disabled veterans may exempt part of one property they own. The Comptroller's scale by VA disability rating runs like this:

  • Rating of 10 to 29 percent: a deduction as high as $5,000
  • Rating of 30 to 49 percent: as high as $7,500
  • Rating of 50 to 69 percent: as high as $10,000
  • Rating of 70 to 100 percent: as high as $12,000

Veterans with a 100 percent rating are fully exempt on the residence homestead. Someone who inherited a Pearland house but is not named on a recorded deed can still apply by giving the appraisal district an ownership affidavit, the death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

What if I sell a Pearland house with unpaid taxes?

Back tax follows the lot rather than the seller. The lien starts each January 1, delinquent amounts block clear title for a buyer, and whoever held the house on that date can still be sued for that year's bill after selling.

Penalty and interest can be waived in many cases when the tax is paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency and a written request arrives before day 181. Residence homestead owners can ask for a payment plan, and some collectors stretch it to 36 months. Someone who appeals an appraisal must still pay the undisputed amount before the delinquency date.

After a suit and sale, a homestead can be bought back for two years once the purchaser's deed is filed, and other land for 180 days. Surplus proceeds stay claimable by the former owner for two years.

What do Census figures show about Pearland?

The Census Bureau counted 91,252 Pearland residents in 2010 and 125,828 in 2020, and estimates 129,930 for July 2025. Land area is 48.67 square miles, which made the 2020 density about 2,585 per square mile.

Homeowners make up 76.2 percent of the 44,410 households counted for 2020-2024. A middle-of-the-range owned home is worth $356,300, and the median household brings in $118,842. Mortgage holders spend $2,611 a month at the median, renters pay $1,860, and a typical worker spends 32.7 minutes commuting. Nearly half of adults hold at least a bachelor's degree, at 47.1 percent.

Is Pearland in Brazoria County or Fort Bend County?

Both. The Comptroller's directories list the City of Pearland as a taxing unit in the Brazoria and the Fort Bend appraisal districts, so your parcel's location decides which district appraises it.

When is Pearland property tax delinquent?

Anything unpaid after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, the day penalty and interest start. By the first of July the penalty stands at 12 percent.

What rate does Pearland charge for 2026?

The 2026 notice shows two benchmark figures, $0.637892 and $0.693542, and no adopted rate. Your bill or the city finance office will show the rate actually set.

Can I pay Pearland property tax in installments?

Yes. Any owner may pay half by the end of November and half by the end of June. A homestead owner who is 65 or older or disabled may use four installments, and a homestead owner who is behind may request a plan lasting as long as 36 months.

Who owes the current year's tax after a Pearland sale?

The person who owned on January 1 carries the legal liability for that year. Closings usually prorate the year between buyer and seller and clear earlier delinquent years from the proceeds.

Treat January 31 as a cliff. Statements arrive in the fall, and the account stays clean through the end of January. On February 1 the collector starts adding charges, and the balance keeps swelling through the summer.

Odessa adds a few city rules a seller meets before listing. Residential building permits come from the Building Inspection division at 411 W. 8th Street, by phone at 432-335-3214 or through the online portal. The release explains that the rate did not change, but a higher average taxable value moves the city share of the bill up by about $70 a year. It also notes new water and wastewater rates from October 1, with the monthly base charge on a 3/4-inch meter rising from $8 to $9.60.

The city describes the budget as a continuation of a multi-year plan to protect essential services, strengthen its workforce and keep investing in public safety, infrastructure and economic development. It also adds employee pay adjustments and continued work on voter-approved bond projects. Those priorities are what the tax rate pays for, alongside water, sewer, drainage and trash fees that appear on separate city bills.

These figures cover the city only. Richardson ISD, the county and any other unit send their own charges through the county tax office.

Does Richardson offer a homestead exemption?

Richardson does not offer the optional percentage homestead exemption, so nothing appears for it on the city's line of a Collin or Dallas County statement. The city's FAQ explains that only school districts must grant a homestead exemption, and that other units choose whether to adopt an optional one.

The city does give a senior exemption, which the budget release puts at $160,000. Apply through the appraisal district for the county where your property lies, not through city hall. The state-level breaks sit on top of that:

  • Richardson ISD, like every school district, must give the $140,000 residence homestead exemption.
  • Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, shield $60,000 more from school tax.
  • After the first qualifying year, a homestead's appraised value is limited to a 10 percent annual rise.
  • Filing closes before May 1. A buyer closing after New Year's Day may still claim for the rest of the year when the seller held no exemption.
  • A 100 percent VA rating brings a full exemption on the residence homestead.

What penalties apply to late Richardson property tax?

Charges begin the day after January 31. The first of February brings a six percent penalty plus one percent interest, then the penalty rises a point each month and reaches 12 percent in July. Interest never stops accruing at a point a month. A unit that retains a collection attorney can add a fee of up to 20 percent.

Spreading payment is possible: half by the end of November and half by the end of June. Homestead owners who are 65 or older or disabled can use four installments, and a late installment draws a six percent penalty. Waiver of penalty and interest is possible if the tax is paid by the 21st day after the owner learns of the delinquency and a written request goes in before day 181.

An appraisal protest follows its own track. The filing deadline is May 15, or the 30th day after delivery of the notice when that comes later. While the dispute goes on, pay at least the undisputed tax before February 1.

What does back tax mean for a Richardson sale?

A tax lien forms each January 1 and stays on the property through any sale. Expect the title company to require past-due amounts at closing, since no buyer receives clear title until they are cleared. Whoever owned on that January 1 is also still liable for the year's bill.

Utility accounts matter at the same time. Richardson's utility customer service line is 972-744-4120, and the 2026-27 budget changed the way residential wastewater is calculated, using only the prior year's November through February water use and leaving out the highest month. A seller who is closing should call utility customer service about ending the account so the final bill is settled. Customers over 65 with a 3/4-inch or 1-inch meter keep the old $8 base charge.

Street work can touch a listing too. The city reported sanitary sewer rehabilitation near the Promenade Shopping Center off Coit Road and in the Berkner Park neighborhood, using pipe bursting and pipe lining so that road closures stay minor and fewer construction vehicles are needed.

If a taxing unit sues and sells the house, a former homestead owner can buy it back for two years after the buyer's deed is filed, and other property for 180 days. Heirs selling an inherited Richardson house should first record the matching paperwork: a muniment of title order, an executor's deed, or an affidavit of death with a transfer on death deed.

What do Census figures show about Richardson?

On 28.57 square miles of land, Richardson recorded 119,469 people in 2020, up from 99,223 in 2010. The 2025 estimate of 118,542 is slightly under the 2020 base, a 0.8 percent dip. Density was about 4,182 residents per square mile in 2020.

Richardson is nearly evenly split between owners and renters, with owners at 50.7 percent. Across 45,818 households in the 2020-2024 survey, a typical owned home is worth $431,400 and rent runs $1,857 at the median. Household income reaches $98,111 at the median, 57.0 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and workers commute 23.6 minutes on average. Owners with a mortgage report monthly costs of $2,524, and 79.0 percent of residents were in the same home a year before. Residents 65 or older make up 13.0 percent of the population, the group the city's senior exemption is aimed at, and children under 18 make up 20.2 percent.

Which county do I pay Richardson property tax to?

Use the tax office of the county that holds your parcel. Part of Richardson is in Dallas County and part in Collin County, and the city's site gives the address and phone for each office.

What is Richardson's property tax rate?

The city's 2026-27 rate is $0.54218 per $100 of assessed valuation, held unchanged by the budget the council adopted. Richardson ISD, the county and other units add their own rates.

Does Richardson have a senior exemption?

Yes. The city's budget announcement says the $160,000 senior property tax exemption continues in 2026-27. Ask the appraisal district for your county how to apply.

When does Richardson property tax become delinquent?

February 1 of the year following the tax year. The city's FAQ shows it with 2026 tax, billed in October 2026 and delinquent on February 1, 2027.

Can I sell a Richardson house that has back taxes?

Yes. Past-due tax is usually taken out of the proceeds at closing so the buyer gets a clear title. Because the January 1 owner remains liable, the settlement sheet should spell out who covers which part of the year.

Homeowners may qualify to split the bill: one payment by November 30 and the balance by June 30 of the next year, under the calendar the Comptroller publishes, which the Smith County office can confirm for your bill.

Texas requires school districts to subtract $140,000 from a homestead's value, and owners 65 and over or disabled receive another $60,000 off the school district value. The application deadline for most exemptions is before May 1 with the appraisal district.

The appraisal review board accepts protests through May 15, or through the 30th day after delivery of your notice when that falls later. Notices for single-family homesteads are mailed around April 1, and the board starts hearing protests around mid May.

Each January 1 a lien arises for that year's tax, and the owner on that date is liable for the year's tax. Your sale contract decides who covers which part of the year's bill at closing.

Jefferson CAD's own web page warns about companies that mail a designation-of-homestead form and charge a fee to file an application that costs nothing. You can file directly with the district, even for earlier years in some cases.

After the appraisal review board rules, you can appeal to district court, choose binding arbitration, or take a value over $1,000,000 to the State Office of Administrative Hearings. On February 1 a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest attach, and penalty rises 1 percent a month to 12 percent on July 1. Attorney fees can add up to 20 percent.

Apply with the Jefferson Central Appraisal District, which takes homestead applications directly at no cost. The house must be yours and your principal residence, and you cannot claim a second homestead elsewhere.

Victoria by the numbers

Who sets and collects property tax on a Victoria home?

Three separate offices touch a Victoria bill. The Victoria Central Appraisal District values the property, each taxing unit picks its own rate, and the Victoria County Tax Office mails the statement and takes the money.

The Census Bureau counts Victoria at 66,500 people for mid-2025, a gain of 1.5% since 2020, on roughly 37 square miles. In the 2020 to 2024 survey, owners occupy 57.9% of homes, the median home is valued at $207,100 and median rent is $1,172. Those numbers explain why homestead rules matter here: most bills are on modest homes, so a fixed-dollar school exemption removes a large share of the school value.

The appraisal district's own page lists who does what. It determines values, mails notices of appraised value, handles protests and administers exemptions. The taxing entities set budgets and rates. The tax assessor-collector calculates and distributes bills and collects payment. Inside city limits, one bill can carry county, school, city and sometimes junior college, hospital or road district charges.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address changes: Victoria Central Appraisal District, 2805 N. Navarro St., Suite 300, phone (361) 576-3621, weekdays 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
  • Bills, payments, penalty questions: the Victoria County Tax Office, 205 N. Bridge St., Suite 101, phone (361) 576-3671.
  • City rate and budget questions: the City of Victoria.

What is the Victoria city tax rate?

The city's 2025 rate was $0.4790 per $100 of taxable value, and the city's 2026 meeting notice proposed $0.4538. A city notice posted on September 9, 2026 says the council adopted a rate. The figure on your own statement is the final word.

The city's meeting notice also sets out the voter-approval and no-new-revenue rates. It lists $0.4538 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.4652 as the voter-approval rate for 2026. Those two benchmarks bracket the council's choice.

Source: City of Victoria notice. The table covers the city's share only. Ask the tax office for the combined rate on your account.

What deadlines and late charges apply to a Victoria bill?

The county tax office mails statements in October, and payment is owed on receipt. Nothing is late before February 1, so January 31 is the practical deadline.

The county's explanation: the penalty opens at 6%, climbs a point on the first of each later month, then adds 2 points on July 1 to reach 12%. Interest is separate, at 1% for each month. A payment mailed late in January counts only if the post office postmarks the envelope by January 31. The Comptroller notes that units with collection attorneys may add up to 20 percent more on accounts still open in July.

The county tax office receives the certified roll from the appraisal district by July 25, then combines it with each unit's adopted rate to produce the October statements. The district's calendar lists mid-April for appraisal notices and August to September for rate setting.

  • If no statement arrives by November 1, ask the tax office to mail one. A bill that never arrived does not excuse the tax or release the lien.
  • With an escrow account, put your loan number on any statement that reaches you and forward it to the lender.
  • Lenders have to ask the county for their clients' statements by late August, or the owner may get the bill directly.

How can a Victoria homeowner lower the property tax bill?

File a residence homestead exemption with the appraisal district, and protest the value if the notice looks too high. Both steps happen at the appraisal district, not at the tax office.

A home qualifies for the general exemption when it is the owner's main residence on January 1. Homeowners at 65 and up get an additional exemption, and there are separate exemptions for disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans and their surviving spouses. School districts statewide give a $140,000 homestead exemption, plus $60,000 more to seniors and disabled owners. A taxing unit may also adopt a percentage exemption of its own, so ask which local options apply to Victoria units.

Victoria CAD's exemption page lists what an applicant must supply under House Bill 585:

  • A copy of a Texas driver license or Texas ID card, with the property address matching the address on the license, vehicle registration or a utility bill.
  • A statement that no other homestead is claimed in or outside Texas.
  • Manufactured homes need a statement of ownership and location from the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs.

Active duty military members and their spouses can ask the chief appraiser to waive the address match. The exemption is not an annual application unless the chief appraiser asks you to reapply. Forms are on the district's Forms page, and the district takes completed exemption forms at exemptions@victoriacad.org.

Homesteads also have a state cap of 10% a year on appraised value growth once the first qualifying year has passed. A school tax freeze for seniors and disabled owners can follow them to a replacement Texas homestead.

How do I protest my Victoria appraisal?

Get a notice of protest to the appraisal district by May 15, or by the 30th day after your appraisal notice arrives when that date falls later. The district's taxpayer page links Form 50-132, a guide to filling it out, and the Comptroller's video on presenting a case.

The calendar on that page lists mid-April for the mailing of notices and May 15 for the protest deadline. The district accepts protests at protest@victoriacad.org. If the review board's order still looks wrong, the Comptroller lists court, binding arbitration or the State Office of Administrative Hearings as next steps.

How can I pay Victoria County property tax?

You can pay in person at a county tax office, by mail, by phone or online. Partial payments are accepted, though any balance left after January 31 starts to collect penalty and interest.

  • In person: cash, check, money order, debit or credit card. A convenience fee applies to cards.
  • By phone at 877-253-4085, for Victoria County accounts only. The county lists a 2.30% card fee with a $1 minimum and a flat $0.50 fee for an electronic check.
  • By mail: write the account number and the words "partial payment" on a partial payment.
  • A returned check carries a $30 service charge.

Seniors and disabled homeowners can ask about the four-installment option.

How does a sale change who pays the Victoria tax?

The lien securing each year's tax arrives on January 1 and stays with the house, which is why closing agents pay the year's tax from the seller's funds. The county tax office tells new buyers to check their closing papers, because the title company may have collected from the seller and credited the buyer.

Whoever owned on January 1 stays liable for that year's tax after a sale. Delinquent tax blocks clear title, so a late Victoria account gets paid off from the proceeds. Before listing, get a balance for every unit from the tax office.

A buyer who closes mid-year may qualify for the exemption on the rest of that tax year when the seller never held it.

More questions about Victoria, TX Property Tax Guide

Is the 2026 Victoria city tax rate adopted?

The City of Victoria posted a notice on September 9, 2026 that it adopted a 2026 rate. The city's meeting notice proposed $0.4538 per $100, so confirm the final figure on your statement or with the tax office at (361) 576-3671.

When does Victoria property tax become delinquent?

February 1. A payment postmarked by January 31 counts as on time. After that the county starts the 6% penalty and 1% interest, and the penalty keeps growing each month until it tops out at 12% on July 1.

Which Victoria office changes my value or exemption?

The Victoria Central Appraisal District, reachable at (361) 576-3621. The county tax office sends bills but says the appraisal district makes every change to values, exemptions and account details.

Can I pay only part of my Victoria tax bill?

Yes. The county tax office takes partial payments, but whatever remains after January 31 starts to accrue penalty and interest. Put the account number and the words partial payment on the check.

Does a Victoria buyer owe the seller's unpaid tax?

Unpaid tax stays with the house until it is cleared. The county tells new owners to read their closing papers to see who paid.

Rockwall by the numbers

Where does a Rockwall homeowner send the tax payment?

Pay the Rockwall Central Appraisal District, which both values and collects. Rockwall County's tax office page says that from October 1, 2012 onward the district has handled all county property taxes, which is why a single statement carries every taxing entity.

The district is at 841 Justin Road in Rockwall, phone 972-771-2034. Its website points to a payment portal for tax statements, and a notice there set the 2026 mailing for the week of October 12. A separate truth-in-taxation site lets you search an address and see each entity's proposed and adopted rate.

Having valuation and collection under one roof is handy for a seller. A single request can produce a statement that shows the city, county, school district and any special district balances together.

What is the Rockwall city tax rate?

The council adopts the city rate each September, so read the current number in the truth-in-taxation database or ask city finance. The database lists every unit that taxes your address, which is more useful than a single city figure.

Rockwall County also links a five-year look back at tax rates from its tax office page. Use it to see whether the city, the county and the school district have been nudging rates up or down.

When does a Rockwall tax bill become late?

Statements are mailed in October. Whatever remains after January 31 is delinquent as of February 1, when 6 percent in penalty and 1 percent in interest attach. Each month adds another point of penalty up to 12 percent on July 1, and interest never stops.

A unit that hires a collection attorney may add as much as 20 percent. You can request a waiver of penalty and interest in writing, if the tax is paid within 21 days after you learn of the delinquency and the request lands within 181 days of the delinquency date.

  • Split plan: half by November 30, half by June 30.
  • Seniors and disabled owners: four installments.
  • Homesteads: some collectors allow up to 36 months on old taxes.

The Comptroller's payment guide explains each option.

How do I claim a homestead exemption or protest in Rockwall?

Both go through the appraisal district. File the exemption before May 1, at no charge: the district's home page warns that filing is free and that solicitors who ask for a fee should be avoided.

A protest is timely if filed by May 15 or day 30 after your notice is delivered, whichever is later. The district says review board hearings usually run on weekdays between April and July. Phone or video hearings require a notarized affidavit before you can present evidence. Bring sales from your own street, since countywide medians say little about one house.

School districts must exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, plus $60,000 more for owners 65-plus or disabled, and other units may add their own. The district's exemption breakdown has the local figures, and its home page also links information on Senate Bill 1801, which covers periodic review of homestead exemptions. Read that page for the details.

What do the Census figures say about Rockwall owners?

Rockwall leans toward ownership. Owners occupy 72.5 percent of homes among 18,273 households that average 2.78 people. A mortgage holder's median monthly cost is $2,542, versus $954 for an owner with no loan.

  • 15.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, a group the senior exemption and tax freeze can help.
  • The Census counts 2,539 veterans, some of whom may qualify for the disabled veteran exemption.
  • 86.0 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier, so inventory turns slowly.
  • The city had 47,251 people in April 2020 and 37,490 in April 2010.

Lakeside streets and older blocks near the square can differ a lot from these citywide numbers.

How does Rockwall's land and lake setting affect a sale?

Rockwall County is the smallest in Texas at 147 square miles, and its seat, Rockwall, lies roughly 25 miles northeast of Dallas. The Texas State Historical Association describes cracking, clayey subsoils across the Blackland Prairie, so a seller with recent foundation documentation is better prepared for an inspection.

Lake Ray Hubbard was built in 1969 and 1970 to supply Dallas, and it now covers 13.55 percent of the county. Interstate 30 enters from the Dallas County line and runs past Rockwall toward Royse City, feeding the commuter pattern behind the Census mean trip to work of 31.8 minutes.

  • The town was surveyed in 1854 and named for a buried rock wall that diggers struck in 1851.
  • The county was split from Kaufman County in 1873 because the old seat was inconvenient for northern residents.
  • Typical rainfall is 38.68 inches a year, and July highs average 96 degrees.

How did Rockwall move from cotton to commuter suburb?

Cotton led the early economy, helped along by a gin built in 1866 and a Missouri, Kansas and Texas rail line in 1886. A new courthouse built through the Work Projects Administration replaced the 1893 building during the Depression.

The shift began once workers started commuting to Dallas around 1940, and by 1967 the county joined the Dallas metropolitan statistical area. Interstate 30 opened in the late 1950s. By 2014 the county counted 87,809 people, many drawn by large homes near the lake. That history explains why newer subdivisions, municipal utility districts and public improvement districts sit beside farm roads and older homes on the same tax roll.

What are MUDs and PIDs on a Rockwall tax statement?

They are special districts that can add their own charge to the bill. The appraisal district's home page offers a MUD FAQ and a guide to public improvement districts for owners who want the basics.

If your neighborhood is inside one, the levy appears as its own line. A buyer's agent will look for it because it raises ongoing ownership cost. Ask the district which special districts cover your address, and request the current balance before you list.

How are unpaid Rockwall taxes settled when I sell?

Each year, Texas law lets a tax claim attach to the property on January 1, and that claim follows the house to a new owner. Whoever held title that day may also be pursued personally. Before funding, the escrow officer collects a payoff figure from the appraisal district and wires it out of the buyer's money.

The county clerk files the deed. The clerk manual puts the first page at $5.00 and each added page at $4.00. An heir whose name is on no recorded deed can hand the district an affidavit of ownership interest to get the homestead exemption.

More questions about Rockwall, TX Property Tax Guide

Who collects Rockwall property tax?

The appraisal district collects it, and one combined statement covers every entity. County materials date that setup to October 1, 2012.

When is a Rockwall tax bill delinquent?

On February 1. Any balance left after January 31 picks up 6 percent in penalty and 1 percent in interest, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

What does it cost to file a Rockwall homestead exemption?

Nothing. The district stresses that the filing is free and cautions against paying a solicitor. Aim to file before May 1.

Why is Rockwall County so small?

Kaufman County's seat was a hard trip for northern residents, so the state formed Rockwall County in 1873. It spans 147 square miles, with Rockwall as its seat from the start.

Can I sell a Rockwall house with taxes owed?

Yes. Penalties, interest and tax are all cleared when the sale funds. Ask the appraisal district for a written payoff first.

Galveston by the numbers

Which office mails the tax statement for a house in Galveston?

The Galveston County Tax Office bills and collects for the City of Galveston, for Galveston ISD, for Galveston College and for the county itself, so most island owners get a single statement that covers several taxing units. Every dollar on it goes to a local unit rather than to the state.

Two offices matter. The Galveston Central Appraisal District appraises every parcel at its January 1 market value and rules on exemption claims. Its customer service desk takes mail at 9850 Emmett F. Lowry Expressway, Suite A101, Texas City, Texas 77591, and call (409) 935-1980. The tax office collects the money, accepts mail at 722 21st Street, Galveston, TX 77550, and answers questions about balances at (409) 766-2481.

The county tax office says only the appraisal district can change ownership or mailing address on a parcel. The tax office will pass a correction along as a courtesy, but a seller who moved or a buyer who just closed should file the change with the appraisal district so the next statement reaches the right person.

What rate did Galveston's council adopt for 2026?

The city adopted a 2026 rate of $0.416273 per $100 of property value when City Council approved the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. The city's news release describes that figure as the no-new-revenue rate, meaning the rate that raises the same revenue as the prior year from properties taxed in both years.

The same release puts operating funds at about $250.1 million, adds a five-year capital plan of roughly $347.8 million, and notes that the fiscal year runs October 1 to September 30. It also says the city's finances swing with the seasons, a pattern that suits an island where hotel and restaurant sales hit $672,706 thousand in 2022, by Census figures.

The city rate is only one slice. Galveston ISD, the county, Galveston College and any special district such as a navigation or drainage district each adopt their own rate. The Galveston Central Appraisal District lists every unit that taxes a given parcel on its property page, and the Texas.gov property tax database shows proposed and adopted rates during late summer.

What is the Galveston payment deadline, and how do late fees build up?

Statements are mailed in October, and the bill must be paid by the end of January. Taxes still unpaid on February 1 are delinquent, and the county tax office points out that a postmark after January 31 triggers penalties unless you use one of the payment plans below.

On February 1 Texas tacks on 6 percent in penalty and 1 percent in interest. The penalty then climbs a point per month until July 1, when it stands at 12 percent, and interest keeps accruing every month without a ceiling. A collection attorney hired by the unit may add another charge, capped at 20 percent. A written waiver request goes to the county's Penalty and Interest Committee, and the state allows waivers in limited cases if the owner pays within 21 days of finding out the tax is delinquent.
