Paying online by e-check or card costs a fee. You can also pay by phone at 1-800-420-1663 or leave a payment in the yellow drop box at any full-time office. Payments by mail should use the 722 21st Street address, because the county warns that the postal service does not always recognize the Moody Avenue address.

How can a Galveston homeowner lower the tax bill?

Start with the homestead exemption, which the appraisal district offers to owners who occupy the house. Apply by mail, online or in person, and expect a decision within 90 days of receipt. The general filing deadline is before May 1.

  • The school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and a homeowner who is over 65 or has a disability gets $60,000 more off the school tax base.
  • A local percentage exemption is optional, topping out at 20 percent of value with a floor of $5,000.
  • Seniors and disabled owners receive a school tax ceiling that can move with them to another Texas homestead, and a spouse who survives at 55 or older can keep it.
  • Disabled veterans may qualify for exemptions that scale with the VA rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total homestead exemption.

After the exemption is in place, a homestead's appraised value is limited to a 10 percent annual increase. A value protest is due May 15 unless the notice arrived late, in which case you get 30 days from delivery. The county tax office also lists a tax deferral affidavit (state form 50-126) among its forms for owners who qualify.

How do Galveston's housing numbers read in the Census?

QuickFacts shows a city that has held steady in size: 53,636 people in the July 2025 estimate against 53,695 in the 2020 count, on 41.05 square miles of land. An owner lives in 46.2 percent of housing units, which leaves most of them to renters.

The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $326,000, the middle monthly rent is $1,298, and household income sits at $55,631 (2020 to 2024 survey). Roughly one resident in five, 20.9 percent, is 65 or older, and that age group is the one eligible for the school tax ceiling and quarterly installments.

There are 25,198 households of about 1.98 people each. Workers spend 20.2 minutes on average getting to work,, and the Census counts 2,982 veterans living in the city.

How do unpaid taxes affect selling a house in Galveston?

Unpaid tax follows the house into a sale. Each January 1 a lien secures that year's tax on the parcel, and whoever owned it that day stays liable after any later transfer.

Ask the Galveston County Tax Office for a current statement before listing, and check whether a mortgage servicer already paid the bill through escrow. The county explains that a mortgage code only appears after a lender requests the statement, and it suggests signing up for e-statements in the first year after a payoff or refinance so the bill is not missed.

  • On closing day the title company usually subtracts back taxes, penalties and interest from the seller's check.
  • Someone buying after New Year's Day can still claim the homestead exemption for part of that year when the seller never held it.
  • An owner who cannot cover the bill may ask about a payment agreement, available after February 1, before deciding to sell.

Owing back taxes, needing storm repairs or having tenants in place need not block an as-is sale to an investor. Obtain the payoff figure in writing first, so the closing statement shows the tax paid and the lien cleared.

More questions about Galveston, TX Property Tax Guide

Where does the money go when I pay tax on a Galveston house?

The Galveston County Tax Office gathers payment for the city, Galveston ISD, the county and several other units on a single statement, then passes each unit its share. Statements arrive in October.

What is the tax rate adopted by the City of Galveston for 2026?

The city's figure is $0.416273 per $100 of value, set along with the FY2027 budget on September 18, 2026. School, county and special district rates are added to reach your total.

Can I split my Galveston property tax bill?

Yes. Paying half by November 30 leaves the second half open until June 30, with no penalty or interest. Senior, disabled and disabled-veteran homesteads can choose four installments instead, due at the end of January, March, May and July.

By what date should a Galveston owner apply for the homestead exemption?

File with the appraisal district ahead of May 1 for the year you want it. The district acts on an application within 90 days of receiving it and will tell you if you do not qualify.

Does a sale make a tax lien on my Galveston house disappear?

No. The lien stays on the parcel until the balance is cleared. The title company settles it out of the seller's funds, so request a payoff statement from the county tax office first.

The city share is one slice of the bill. County, school and special district rates share the same statement. The tax formula printed on the notice is the tax rate times the taxable value divided by 100, with exemptions already removed from the taxable value.

They differ sharply. The city's taxpayer impact statement lists the median homestead taxable value in each county portion of Katy.

A seller with tax owed on a Katy house has a plain path. Get the payoff statement from the right county, read the city's adopted rate on its tax page, and tell the title company which of the three counties holds the parcel. The county decides which collector, which appraisal district and which protest board apply, and a wrong guess costs time.

What happens if a Katy tax bill is paid late?

The cutoff is January 31, and the penalty starts February 1: 6 percent plus 1 percent interest, both growing through July. The city's tax page adds a warning that a bill you never received leaves the tax, the due date and the lien exactly where they were.

Each January 1 a lien attaches to the house for that year's tax, which is why a Katy sale cannot close cleanly until the year's bill is settled or credited. Ask the county that bills the address, Fort Bend, Harris or Waller, for a payoff statement, and give it to the title company early.

An owner who fell behind has two tools. A penalty waiver request goes in writing within 181 days of the delinquency date, and a collector may offer a payment plan.

How can a Katy owner lower the bill?

The biggest levers sit with the appraisal district and the exemptions you file for. Because Katy runs through three counties, a Katy owner deals with Fort Bend, Harris or Waller for each of them. These are the main ones:

  • The school district homestead exemption of $140,000, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A city or county exemption, if the unit adopted one. Texas lets a unit set up to 20 percent of value with a $5,000 floor, and the Exemption Eligibility tab on Katy's tax page gives the city's terms.
  • The 10 percent yearly limit on homestead value growth, which begins after the exemption is first granted.
  • A protest to the appraisal review board, usually due in mid-May.

A buyer who closes after January 1 can claim the homestead exemption at once for that year when the seller never held it.

How did Katy's 2026 notice describe the rate change?

The notice said the effective rate would rise 0.66 percent, which raises maintenance and operations tax on a $100,000 home by about $2.42. The proposed $0.420000 sits between the no-new-revenue rate of $0.407051 and the voter-approval rate of $0.443092, so no election was required. The notice records every voting council member in favor and none against, with the mayor present and not voting.

A separate taxpayer impact statement for the September 14, 2026 council meeting compares city tax bills on the median homestead: $1,559.34 under the current budget, $1,552.64 under the proposed budget and $1,504.77 at the no-new-revenue rate. These are the city's published estimates for the median homestead, and your own bill depends on your taxable value.

The city sets the rate, but the three appraisal districts set the values. If your value rises while the rate falls, your city bill can still move up.

How do I pay a Katy property tax bill?

Pay the collector for the county where your house sits. Fort Bend County takes online payment by card or electronic check. Its page prints a card fee of 2.29 percent of the total with a $2.75 minimum, no fee for electronic checks, and a 3.95 percent fee on business and international cards. It deposits post-dated checks on receipt, so do not date a check for later.

Questions to the Fort Bend office go to FBCTaxInfo@fortbendcountytx.gov or 281-341-3710. Harris and Waller owners use their own county's collector, as the city page lists. If your lender pays from escrow, look up the account online and confirm the payment posted before January 31.

The city's notice also points owners to Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes, which links to the local property tax database showing proposed rates and hearings for each unit that taxes your address.

More questions about Katy, TX Property Tax Guide

Who collects the City of Katy property tax?

Your county's tax office collects it, because the city charge rides on the county bill. Fort Bend, Harris and Waller each have a payment location on the city's tax page.

What rate did Katy propose for 2026?

The notice proposed $0.420000 per $100 of valuation, compared with $0.425000 for 2025. Look at the adopted rate on the city's tax page, then add the county, school and special district rates.

When does Katy tax go delinquent?

After January 31. February 1 brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent monthly interest, and bills arrive around October 1.

Does Katy offer its own homestead exemption?

The city's tax page has an Exemption Eligibility tab with its terms. The state school exemption is $140,000 on top of that, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.

Can I protest my Katy appraisal?

Yes, through the appraisal review board of the county that holds your house. The usual deadline falls in mid-May, or 30 days after a late notice.
